decision_conditions:
<div>The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting and design would cause severe harm to the neighbouring occupiers. Specifically, the proposed development would unacceptably result in a material loss of outlook to the occupiers of no.806 Rainham South, and introduce significant levels of overbearing, overshadowing, loss of outlook, and loss of daylight.&nbsp; The proposed development would therefore constituting unneighbourly development and contrary to:<br></div><div><br></div><div><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
National Planning Policy Framework </span>National Planning Policy Framework
(NPPF) (MHCLG, 2024)<o:p></o:p></p><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">- Policy
D4 of the London Plan (March 2021);</span></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; line-height: 107%; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">- The Residential
Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012);<o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal">









</p><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of </span>The London Borough of Barking and
Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037: (September 2024)<o:p></o:p></p></div>

<div>The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting, design, bulk and mass would be an undesirable addition, to the existing dwelling. The first floor side extension fails to maintain a gap between the subject dwelling and neighbouring dwelling, failing to preserve the existing character of the street scape and pattern of development. The first floor rear extension would be a significant addition to the site,&nbsp; failing to remain within the 45 degree angle as taken from the corner of the neighbouring dwelling, and resulting in the site appearing as overdeveloped. As such, the cumulative impact of the proposal would cause undue harm to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area. The proposal is therefore contrary tot he following policies which seek to ensure that development recognises local character and promotes good design:&nbsp;&nbsp;</div><div><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
